captions.detailed: A woodworking quick-release vise designed for a carpenter's bench. It features a dark-colored fixed rear jaw, a sliding front jaw of the same color, and two long metallic guide bars extending outwards. A rotating screw handle with wooden-colored end caps sits at the front, while a small dark quick-release lever is positioned on the side of the main housing. The front jaw slides prismatically along the guide bars, the screw handle rotates continuously, and the quick-release lever tilts on its short side pivot.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a woodworking quick-release workbench vise. The assembly must include a fixed rear jaw, a sliding front jaw that moves prismatically along two parallel guide bars, a continuously rotating lead-screw handle with wooden-textured cylindrical ends, and a small quick-release lever that rotates on a short side pivot near the screw housing.
captions.factory: Construct the base/fixed jaw using a box primitive and attach a wooden mounting block on its back. Create the sliding front jaw as another box that translates along the Y-axis. Model the guide bars and main screw as long cylinder primitives extending from the front jaw. Build the screw handle with a central cylinder cross-bar and two wooden-colored cylindrical end caps. Finally, construct the quick-release lever from a small cylinder pivot and an angled arm, and define the prismatic, continuous, and revolute joints with appropriate motion limits and axes.
